items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-05
items.q: Fat used to come over there and sit in and play with us a lot of times.

ctx.x: Like to do it. Uh, who all did you get offers from? What were some of the different people?

I got an offer from Earl Heinz. Who want me to come up? Uh. Yeah. Got off. Uh. Oliver wanted me to come up there with him. I wouldn't leave though. And then we had this fellow, Fat Wallace. He wanted me to come up with him. But I wasn't going no way.
Well, how did Fat Wallace know you? Fat used to come down here often.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: INTERVIEWER: You play with him much? ... INTERVIEWEE: Jam or anything? Oh yeah, I jam with him.

ctx.x: What about, uh, Fat Wallace? You ever know him? Sure, I know Fat. You play with him much? No.

Jam or anything? Oh yeah, I jam with him. Yeah. Oh yeah, I jam with him. When he coming out of the lyrics, the lyrics to you. Yeah, I jam with him. Did you ever get any offers from those guys? Yes, in my twenties I got a lot of offers. Who were some of the guys? Jimmy Lundford. I got offers from Jimmy. There's another guy named Boy, I can't think of his name now. He come to me directly. Yeah, well. And then late years you played a lot of grass band work on Hope too, wasn't it? Yeah, I played with, uh, but there…

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-05
items.q: I know I had been playing with the, Fate on the jam sessions, Fate Marvel.

ctx.x: Well, he had a little bit of air on the piano. But play. Ooh, he could play some piano. And never was sober. Never was sober. He stayed right there in the same hotel with us. He wake up in the morning and get drunk. Get drunk when he eat. Twelve o'clock he get drunk. Go to work he's drunk. Come from work he's drunk. But play. Never was late on the job. And never went to sleep. Never went to sleep. But he'd be drunk. Played everything you put in front of him and what you don't put in front of him he played. He was…
